title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday for renovation; similar closures reduce weekly sales by ~10-15% based on past closures in the same store.

drivers.name: Price increase (+6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Past 30% off promotions lifted sales to x1.4 (noise-adjusted); reverse effect expected for price increase. One past x0.87 reading at similar price point suggests ~13% drop, shrunk to -6% due to low evidence.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.7. The target week has no event, but a 6.2% price increase to $12.03 and a store closure on Monday. Price increases reduce demand; past 30% off promotions lifted sales to x1.52 (noise-adjusted x1.4), but price hikes have the opposite effect. The week after a promotion typically sees x0.76 sales (noise-adjusted x1.0), suggesting a post-promo dip. However, no promotion occurred recently, so no pantry-loading effect. The store closure reduces sales, especially on Monday, likely cutting 10-15% of weekly volume. The evidence for price impact is limited to one past price increase (x0.87), but the closure is a strong, named driver. Adjust downward for closure and price, but shrink toward 1.0 due to weak evidence. No other drivers.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 3.6 - 38.4 | 10%-90%: 7.5 - 34.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
